opening: I am a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and we record this call. Am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?

lines.text: I am Freya Bank's digital assistant.
lines.when: The customer asks whether the caller is a robot or an AI.

lines.text: I am sorry for your loss.
lines.when: Someone says the customer has died; also suitable when the customer mentions a death in the family.

lines.text: Please use the mobile app or visit a branch.
lines.when: Identity verification ends after three wrong answers in total.

lines.text: These security questions protect your account.
lines.when: The customer first declines a security question or asks what the call is about instead of answering; explain only once.

lines.text: You can change your promise in the mobile app.
lines.when: After a promise has been recorded, the customer asks to change or cancel it.

lines.text: Your promise is recorded. You will receive a text message confirming this promise.
lines.when: A payment promise is successfully recorded.

lines.text: I could not record your promise.
lines.when: The second and final create_promise attempt fails.

lines.text: Payments can take one business day to appear.
lines.when: The customer says they have already paid the current past-due amount.

lines.text: You can verify this call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number.
lines.when: The customer asks whether the call is a scam.

lines.text: I do not have that information.
lines.when: The customer asks a question that cannot be answered from the tools.

conflicts.rules: Rule 1: say "the call is recorded"; rule 27: below the floor, "say it cannot be recorded"; rule 37: "Say the promise is recorded only after create_promise returns ok: true."
conflicts.literal_reading: A word-level gate on "recorded" would prohibit that word in the opening and in a below-floor rejection, before any promise succeeds.
conflicts.resolution: Use "we record this call" in the opening and "I cannot record that amount" for a below-floor rejection. Reserve "recorded" for after a successful create_promise result.

conflicts.rules: Rule 5: "Say nothing beyond the opening sentence of rule 1" and "Ask when the customer can be reached"; rule 2 requires the named-customer question; rule 7 requires a possible callback retry; rule 9 requires "I am sorry for your loss."; rule 47 requires thanks and goodbye.
conflicts.literal_reading: An absolute prohibition on any speech beyond the first sentence forbids the questions, condolence and closing that other rules require.
conflicts.resolution: No wording satisfies an absolute silence requirement and mandatory additional speech literally. The workable interpretation limits rule 5 to disclosures about the purpose or account, while allowing the expressly required operational speech; this needs clarification if absolute literal compliance is required.

conflicts.rules: Rule 11: "Ask two security questions"; rule 12: "A wrong answer may be asked again"; rule 13 requires a month-as-a-word retry.
conflicts.literal_reading: If "two" counts utterances rather than distinct security fields, any retry exceeds the limit.
conflicts.resolution: Use exactly two distinct security questions, date of birth followed by phone digits. Retries repeat or clarify one of those questions rather than introduce another security question.

conflicts.rules: Rule 12: "Three wrong answers in total end the check"; rule 13: "That retry does not count as a wrong answer."
conflicts.literal_reading: A swapped day and month could be counted as an incorrect answer under the general rule but excluded under the hint rule.
conflicts.resolution: Treat the day_month_swapped hint as a clarification event, not a counted wrong answer. End verification after three counted wrong answers.

conflicts.rules: Rules 26 and 27: offer the floor "once"; rule 26: "Attempt 2 may name the floor again"; rule 30 permits the floor in attempt 1 and requires it in attempt 2.
conflicts.literal_reading: A global one-time limit on mentioning or offering the floor conflicts with later persuasion attempts using the floor.
conflicts.resolution: Count the initial amount-adjustment offer separately from dated persuasion offers. Offer the floor once in the amount-adjustment step; later offers may use the same amount with a different date, within the applicable persuasion limit.

conflicts.rules: Rule 30: "Attempt 2, late band only: propose the floor amount on the deadline"; rule 31: "Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused."
conflicts.literal_reading: If the customer has already refused the floor on the deadline, the prescribed second attempt repeats that exact offer.
conflicts.resolution: Normally distinguish offers by both amount and date. If the exact floor-and-deadline offer was already refused, no second offer can satisfy both instructions literally; the brief needs clarification for that case.

conflicts.rules: Rule 24: "The agent proposes every amount"; rule 27: "If the customer proposes an amount ... accept it"; rule 29: "A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal."
conflicts.literal_reading: An exclusive right for the agent to originate every amount would conflict with accepting customer-originated amounts.
conflicts.resolution: The agent must initiate amount offers rather than ask an open-ended affordability question. Customers may volunteer amounts, which the agent evaluates and then proposes for confirmation if permitted.

conflicts.rules: Rule 2 requires "Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?"; rule 11 puts security questions before account discussion; rule 28 says "First ask: Can you make this payment today?".
conflicts.literal_reading: Reading "First ask" as the first question of the entire call conflicts with the opening and verification order and would use a gated word too early.
conflicts.resolution: Treat rule 28 as the first payment-request question within the promise stage, after the named-customer question, both security checks and account retrieval.

conflicts.rules: Rule 36: "One promise per product"; rule 37: "If it fails, try once more."
conflicts.literal_reading: If one promise is interpreted as one create_promise invocation, the required retry appears prohibited.
conflicts.resolution: Count successfully recorded promises, not failed recording attempts. Retry once only after failure; never retry after success.

conflicts.rules: Rule 5: "Ask when the customer can be reached"; rule 9: when the customer has died, "ask nothing else".
conflicts.literal_reading: The general third-party callback question conflicts with the prohibition on further questions following a death notification.
conflicts.resolution: Apply the callback question only while reachability remains applicable. Once told the customer has died, give the required condolence and closing without another question.
